extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), corporate finance/accounting teams, corporate counsel, auditors and transaction/advisory professionals preparing SEC filings for business combinations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when and what financial information and disclosures a registrant must file with the SEC for acquisitions, probable acquisitions, and dispositions of businesses under S‑X (including Rules 3‑05, 11‑01 and 6‑11) and related Form 8‑K/registration/proxy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating substantially all revenues from leasing of real property requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an acquired business meets this requirement depends on the type of revenues it generates from its real property. Real estate operations are premised on the continuity and predictability of cash flows ordinarily associated with commercial and apartment property leasing, and generally include shopping centers and malls. In contrast, businesses that are more susceptible to variations in costs and revenues over shorter periods due to market and managerial factors do not meet this requirement and therefore are not considered real estate operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of businesses that generally meet the requirement: shopping centers and malls. Examples that do not meet the requirement: nursing homes, hotels, motels, golf courses, auto dealerships and equipment rental operations (because of greater variability of costs/revenues). The analysis focuses on the type/continuity/predictability of revenue streams from the real property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods required for abbreviated financial statements when acquiring a significant real estate operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of periods for which abbreviated financial statements are filed when a registrant acquires a significant real estate operation (for Form 8‑K and registration/proxy statements other than on Form S‑4/F‑4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance: Does not exceed 20% = None. Exceeds 20% = Most recent audited fiscal year and most recent unaudited interim period (no comparative interim period of the prior year is required). See Chapter 5 for period requirements for Form S‑4/F‑4 registration or merger proxy statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of historical abbreviated financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical abbreviated financial statements should include an audited statement of revenues and certain expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenses not expected to be comparable to future operations may be excluded, such as mortgage interest; leasehold rental; depreciation; amortization; corporate overhead; and income taxes. Other basic financial statements (e.g., statement of cash flows) are not required for abbreviated statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma financial information requirement (S‑X Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information is required in accordance with S‑X Article 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are also specific disclosure and supplemental information requirements associated with S‑X Article 11 (see Chapter 8 for more detail). Ensure compliance with S‑X Article 11 presentation and disclosure rules when pro forma information is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of S‑X Rule 6‑11 to registered investment companies and business development companies
rubrics_metrics.description: S‑X Rule 6‑11 (not S‑X Rule 3‑05) applies when certain investment funds acquire other investment funds, or such acquisitions are probable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants subject to Rule 6‑11: Registered investment companies and Business development companies. Types of acquisitions subject to Rule 6‑11 include acquisition of an investment company (section 3(a) of the 1940 Act); a business development company; a company that would be an investment company but for exclusions under sections 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7); or any private account managed by an investment adviser. Significance tests: the asset test does not apply; modified versions of the investment and income tests apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: When financial statements are required for an acquired fund (decision tree)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of whether financial statements must be filed for an acquired fund and which periods must be presented depends on facts such as whether securities are being registered for fund security holders, and significance thresholds (e.g., >20%, aggregate >50%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If securities are being registered to be offered to the security holders of the fund to be acquired → financial statements specified in Rule 3‑01 and 3‑02, or Rule 3‑18 for the fund to be acquired, plus required supplemental information. If not registering securities, evaluate significance: e.g., if acquired (or to be acquired) fund is significant >20% then financial statements and supplemental information required; if aggregate impact since most recent audited balance sheet is >50% then additional periods may be required. If the acquired fund is subject to Rule 3‑18, file the periods described in Rule 3‑18. See Chapter 9 decision tree for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse acquisitions and shell companies — special considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisitions structured as reverse acquisitions or involving public shell companies may require special consideration to determine how and whether S‑X Rule 3‑05 (and related rules) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such scenarios may result in the identification of a predecessor to the registrant and can affect which financial statements and historical disclosures are required. Evaluate transaction structure carefully to determine reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and content rules for abbreviated financial statements (decision tree and special rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant acquires part of an entity that constitutes a business, it may be able to provide abbreviated financial statements instead of full financial statements, depending on several conditions (e.g., whether less than substantially all assets/liabilities were acquired; availability of separate full financial statements; ability to provide carve‑out statements; whether S‑X 3‑05(e) conditions are met; and oil and gas special rules under S‑X 3‑05(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the company acquired less than substantially all assets/liabilities and separate full financial statements exist → provide audited full financial statements in accordance with S‑X Rule 3‑05. If carve‑out statements can be provided → provide audited carve‑out financial statements per S‑X Rule 3‑05. If S‑X 3‑05(e) conditions are met → audited abbreviated financial statements (e.g., statement of assets acquired and liabilities assumed and statement of comprehensive income) may be acceptable. Financial information provided must be of the same period and age as required for full financial statements. If the acquired business is an oil and gas property and S‑X 3‑05(f) applies → audited abbreviated financial statements for the oil and gas property may be provided and can be limited to a statement of revenue and direct expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: When financial information must match periods and age required for full financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial information provided (including abbreviated statements) must be of the same period and age as required for the full financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if providing abbreviated statements, ensure that the periods presented and the 'age' (timeliness) of the financial information match the statutory/testing requirements for the full statements to avoid noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inability to obtain required audited financial statements — waiver or no‑action letter options
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is impossible or would involve unreasonable expense/effort to obtain audited financial statements of an acquired entity for required periods, a registrant may request a waiver or seek an SEC no‑action letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A no‑action letter means the SEC staff agrees not to take action solely as a result of noncompliance with S‑X Rule 3‑05. The SEC staff can waive certain S‑X Rule 3‑05 requirements, for example: providing a statement of revenue and direct expenses in lieu of full financial statements for a recently acquired business; omitting one or more years of historical financial statements; or providing audited financial statements for a shorter time than required under S‑X Rule 3‑05. See Chapter 10 for more detail and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'business' for S‑X Rule 3‑05 purposes (per §210.11‑01(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of whether a business has been acquired should be made in accordance with §210.11‑01(d). Acquisition of a business encompasses acquisition of an interest accounted for under the equity method or fair value option. Acquisitions of a group of related businesses that are probable or have occurred subsequent to the registrant’s latest fiscal year‑end must be treated as a single business acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related businesses may be presented on a combined basis for periods under common control/management. Businesses are deemed related if: (i) under common control or management; (ii) acquisition of one is conditional on acquisition of each other; or (iii) each acquisition is conditioned on a single common event. S‑X Rule 3‑05 does not apply to a real estate operation subject to §210.3‑14 or a business totally held by the registrant prior to consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: S‑X Rule 11‑01(d) presentation requirement — continuity of operations and attributes to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Rule 11‑01, the term 'business' should be evaluated in light of facts and circumstances and whether there is sufficient continuity of the acquired entity’s operations prior to and after the transaction so that disclosure of prior financial information is material to an understanding of future operations. A presumption exists that a separate entity, subsidiary, or division is a business; a lesser component may also constitute a business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Among facts and circumstances to consider: (1) whether the nature of the revenue‑producing activity of the component will remain generally the same as before the transaction; and (2) whether attributes remain with the component after the transaction, e.g., physical facilities; employee base; market distribution system; sales force; customer base; operating rights; production techniques; trade names. These attributes are considered in evaluating continuity but are not an exhaustive definitional list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive guidance on continuity, rebutting the presumption, and procedural practice (obtaining staff concurrence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC’s definition of a business centers on whether there is continuity of the acquired entity’s operations. If revenue‑producing activities remain generally the same after acquisition, it is presumed a business has been acquired. However, a registrant may conclude there is no business if it will not operate the acquired set in the same manner as the prior owner or if there will be a distinct curtailment or change in revenue‑producing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an acquired entity is not producing significant revenue prior to the transaction, judgment is required — registrants consider whether attributes (listed in Rule 11‑01(d)(2)) remain after the transaction. The SEC staff does not view the attributes as a definitive list; lack of one or more attributes does not determine the conclusion. The SEC staff encourages registrants to obtain staff concurrence in advance if they intend to omit financial statements where they have succeeded to a revenue‑producing activity and acquired at least one of the Rule 11‑01(d)(2) attributes. Changes commonly occurring post‑acquisition (new carrying amounts, new financing, management or operational changes) typically do not eliminate the relevance of historical financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical examples applying the continuity test (illustrative assessments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative examples show how continuity analysis is applied: e.g., acquisition of a television station, newspaper printing facility (conversion vs continued operation), food processing business acquired primarily for an FDA certification, food distribution business with retained sales force and managers, acquisition of molecules/early‑stage R&D assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key lessons from examples: change in intended use of facilities or plan not to continue prior operations → lack of continuity → not a 'business' for reporting purposes. Retention of core revenue‑producing attributes (customer service, sales force, mid‑level managers, ongoing operations) supports conclusion that acquisition is a business. Early‑stage assets with no revenue and no separate legal entity holding them generally do not meet definition of a business. Use these examples to test facts/circumstances in analogous transactions.
